themes_detail.label: Wild Animals Invading Parks
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-park complaints spiked to 13 this week—a 316% increase from the 3.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting a sudden wildlife encroachment problem affecting Upper West Side green spaces.
evidence: 13 animal-in-park complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.1 weekly average (316% spike, z-score 7.78)
Highest statistical anomaly in dataset by z-score, indicating unprecedented surge
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request for park reconstruction/upgrades
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept on what species are being reported and why the sudden surge
Talk to park users about safety concerns and whether they're avoiding certain areas
Investigate whether recent construction or park closures are displacing wildlife

themes_detail.label: Lead Contamination Spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead-related complaints jumped to 11 this week, a 91% increase from the 5.8 weekly average, raising urgent questions about drinking water, paint, or soil contamination in residential buildings across the district.
evidence: 11 lead complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.8 weekly average (91% increase, z-score 4.38)
Second-highest recency signal among all spikes
Lead is a public health crisis, especially for children; warrants immediate investigation
reporting_angles: Which buildings or neighborhoods are reporting lead? Are complaints clustered geographically?
Interview DOHMH on whether they've launched inspections or found contamination sources
Talk to families with young children about testing and remediation options available

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees & Branches Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about overgrown trees and branches surged to 5 this week—a 344% spike from the 1.1 weekly average—creating potential safety hazards on streets and sidewalks across the Upper West Side.
evidence: 5 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (344% increase, z-score 3.32)
Emerged this week, tied with animal-in-park for most dramatic recent percentage jump
Overlaps with ongoing street condition complaints (1,059 total), suggesting infrastructure decay pattern
reporting_angles: Walk affected streets with Parks Dept to document hazards and response timelines
Ask Parks about staffing and budget constraints limiting tree maintenance
Interview residents about near-misses or injuries from falling branches

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park-rules violation complaints jumped 300% to 4 this week from a 1.0 weekly average, indicating a sudden shift in park behavior or enforcement activity in community green spaces.
evidence: 4 violation-of-park-rules complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 4.24)
Emerged this week; tied with lead and overgrown trees for most recent anomalies
Complements animal-in-park surge, suggesting broader park-use shift
reporting_angles: What specific violations are being reported? (Off-leash dogs, unauthorized vendors, camping?)
Has Parks Dept increased enforcement, or are residents more aware/vocal?
Is this connected to the animal-in-park spike?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles Accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints hit 13 last week—a 160% spike from the 5.0 weekly average—suggesting a growing problem with derelict cars clogging streets and straining enforcement capacity.
evidence: 13 abandoned vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.0 weekly average (160% increase, z-score 5.06)
One week older than this week's spikes, but still highly anomalous
Fits pattern of street condition deterioration (1,059 total street complaints) and broader infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and Sanitation on removal timelines and resource constraints
Map clusters of abandoned vehicles—are specific neighborhoods affected disproportionately?
Talk to residents about the impact on parking availability and street aesthetics
